Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Sustaining Change — Habits, Systems, and Lifelong Growth.
So, you’ve started making space for what matters most. But how do you make these changes stick, not just for a week or two, but as a real part of your life?
That’s where habits and supportive systems come in. They’re the hidden engine that keep your priorities running smoothly, even as life throws curveballs.
Think of habits as your personal autopilot. Once you’ve got them locked in, they’ll guide your actions almost effortlessly. That’s why building habits that actually support your priorities is so powerful. They take the stress out of constant decision-making and help you keep moving in the right direction.
Here are a few habits that can make a huge difference if you want to live more in that Quadrant II sweet spot:
First, there’s weekly planning. It’s about taking regular time to look at your roles, set your top priorities, and actually schedule the things that matter most. Then, there’s daily reflection. Carve out just a few minutes to check in with your mission and make little tweaks if you need to. And don’t forget about regular renewal—protecting time for rest, learning, and connection. Treat these moments as non-negotiable, just like you would an important meeting.
But habits alone aren’t always enough. That’s where supportive systems come into play.
Maybe you share your goals with an accountability partner—someone you trust to encourage you and give those gentle nudges when you need them. Or you use visual reminders, like a calendar, an alert on your phone, or even an inspiring quote stuck to your mirror. And don’t underestimate the power of periodic reviews. Whether it’s monthly or quarterly, set aside time to check your progress and recalibrate.
Now, here’s something important to remember: living by your first things is a journey, not a finish line you cross once and for all.
Life changes. Kids grow up. Careers shift. What’s most important to you today might look different a few years from now. By staying open to learning and growth, you give yourself the freedom to adapt—while staying true to your core values.
For example, maybe your role as a parent evolves as your kids become more independent, or a new job brings fresh opportunities and challenges. If you regularly check in with your mission and adjust your plans, you’ll keep your actions aligned with what matters most—even as your world changes.
So, as you move forward, focus on building those supportive habits and systems. Give yourself permission to grow, to adjust, and to keep putting first things first—every single day.
